description: 45 tech company logos explained by a brand designer, from Apple, Google, and Microsoft to Spotify, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Stripe.
intro:
Tech logos live on app icons, browser tabs, phones, and billboards, so the best ones are simple enough to read at 16 pixels and distinctive enough to own a color or a shape.

What makes a good tech logo?

Simplicity: the strongest tech logos, from the Apple apple to the Meta loop, work as a single shape on a tiny screen.

Color: many tech brands own one color, like Spotify green, Netflix red, or Stripe purple, so they are recognizable even without the name.

Typography: custom typefaces, like Google's geometric sans or Uber's own font, keep wordmarks consistent across products and languages.

Below are 45 tech company logos in five groups, from Big Tech to AI and startups. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation.

logoResearch.name: Apple
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Apple makes the iPhone, Mac, and iPad, and is one of the most valuable companies in the world.
observations: The bitten apple was designed by Rob Janoff in 1977; the bite gives scale, so it is not mistaken for a cherry.
Once rainbow-striped, the mark has been a single flat color since the late 1990s.

logoResearch.name: Google
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Google is the world's largest search engine and the core of Alphabet.
observations: The 2015 wordmark uses Google's own geometric sans to feel simple and friendly on every screen.
Primary colors with one green letter break the pattern on purpose, a playful signal.

logoResearch.name: Microsoft
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Microsoft makes Windows, Office, Azure, and Xbox.
observations: Four colored squares, introduced in 2012, echo the Windows window and the company's product range.
A quiet grey wordmark lets the colored squares do the work.

logoResearch.name: Amazon
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Amazon is the world's largest online retailer and cloud provider.
observations: The orange arrow is a smile that also points from a to z, everything from A to Z.
A heavy lowercase wordmark keeps the brand approachable.

logoResearch.name: Meta
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Meta is the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
observations: The 2021 symbol is an infinity loop that also reads as an M.
It was designed to work in 3D and motion, hinting at the metaverse.

logoResearch.name: Netflix
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Netflix is the world's largest subscription streaming service.
observations: Bold, condensed red capitals bend slightly like a cinema screen.
The color is so strong that the single letter N works as its app icon.

logoResearch.name: Samsung
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Samsung is a South Korean electronics giant making phones, TVs, and chips.
observations: The blue ellipse, introduced in 1993, suggests the world moving through space.
White, slightly spaced capitals sit inside the tilted ellipse.

logoResearch.name: IBM
logoResearch.verifiedFact: IBM is one of the oldest technology companies, known today for software, consulting, and AI.
observations: Paul Rand's striped logo from 1972 is one of the most famous corporate marks ever designed.
The horizontal stripes suggest speed and help the heavy slab serif feel lighter.

logoResearch.name: Tesla
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Tesla makes electric cars, batteries, and solar products.
observations: The T is shaped like a cross-section of an electric motor, according to Elon Musk.
A widely spaced, angular wordmark below adds a futuristic touch.

logoResearch.name: Salesforce
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Salesforce is the leading customer relationship management software company.
observations: A blue cloud signals that the product lives in the cloud, a bold idea when the company started.
The lowercase wordmark inside the cloud keeps it friendly.

logoResearch.name: Adobe
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Adobe makes Photoshop, Illustrator, and other creative software.
observations: The red A is built from two shapes with a triangle of negative space.
It has been simplified over the years into a bold, flat symbol that works as a tiny icon.

logoResearch.name: Oracle
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Oracle is a giant in databases and enterprise cloud software.
observations: Red capitals with rounded ends give a serious enterprise brand a softer edge.
No symbol is needed; the wordmark is the whole identity.

logoResearch.name: SAP
logoResearch.verifiedFact: SAP is a German company that makes business software used by most large enterprises.
observations: White letters sit in a blue gradient shape with one angled edge.
The angle adds direction to an otherwise very solid, corporate mark.

logoResearch.name: Shopify
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Shopify powers millions of online stores.
observations: The shopping bag with an S explains the product at a glance.
A bold, lowercase italic wordmark adds speed and friendliness.

logoResearch.name: Slack
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Slack is a workplace messaging app owned by Salesforce.
observations: Pentagram's 2019 redesign turned the hashtag into four colored pill shapes.
The simpler symbol fixed the old logo's problems at small sizes and on different backgrounds.

logoResearch.name: Zoom
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zoom is the video meeting app that became a household name in 2020.
observations: Bright blue, rounded lowercase letters feel fast and friendly.
The two o's give the wordmark a built-in rhythm.

logoResearch.name: Dropbox
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Dropbox is a cloud storage and file-sharing service.
observations: An open box built from four blue diamonds explains storage in one simple shape.
The 2017 refresh kept the box but cleaned up the wordmark.

logoResearch.name: Atlassian
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Atlassian makes Jira, Confluence, and Trello.
observations: The blue A also looks like a mountain peak.
Widely spaced capitals give the brand a confident, enterprise feel.

logoResearch.name: Spotify
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Spotify is the world's largest music streaming service.
observations: Three curved lines inside a green circle represent sound waves.
Spotify green is so recognizable that the symbol often appears on its own.

logoResearch.name: Airbnb
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Airbnb is an online marketplace for short-term stays.
observations: The Bélo symbol, introduced in 2014, combines a location pin, a heart, and the letter A.
The pink-red color, called Rausch, makes it stand out among travel brands.

logoResearch.name: Uber
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Uber is a ride-hailing and delivery company.
observations: Since 2018 the brand has used a simple black wordmark set in its own typeface.
Dropping the symbol made the brand clear and consistent across its many services.

logoResearch.name: Instagram
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Instagram is Meta's photo and video sharing app.
observations: The hand-lettered script wordmark feels personal and creative.
It pairs with the gradient camera app icon, which carries the brand's color.

logoResearch.name: YouTube
logoResearch.verifiedFact: YouTube is the world's largest video platform, owned by Google.
observations: The red rounded rectangle with a white triangle is a universal play button.
The condensed wordmark sits next to the icon without competing.

logoResearch.name: TikTok
logoResearch.verifiedFact: TikTok is a short-video app owned by ByteDance.
observations: The music note reflects the app's roots in music and lip-sync videos.
Cyan and red offsets create a glitchy, concert-light effect.

logoResearch.name: Pinterest
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Pinterest is a visual discovery and inspiration platform.
observations: The P is drawn to look like a pin, the core action of the product.
A red script wordmark keeps the brand warm and personal.

logoResearch.name: WhatsApp
logoResearch.verifiedFact: WhatsApp is the world's most used messaging app, owned by Meta.
observations: A phone handset inside a speech bubble explains messaging and calling at once.
WhatsApp green is instantly recognizable on home screens.

logoResearch.name: Snapchat
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Snapchat is a camera and messaging app made by Snap Inc.
observations: The ghost hints at disappearing messages, the app's original big idea.
Bright yellow is unusual for a tech brand and impossible to miss.

logoResearch.name: Nvidia
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Nvidia makes graphics and AI chips and is one of the most valuable companies in the world.
observations: The custom, heavy wordmark has angular letters that feel technical and fast.
Nvidia also uses a green eye symbol, but the wordmark works strongly on its own.

logoResearch.name: Intel
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Intel is one of the world's largest chipmakers.
observations: The 2020 logo simplified the wordmark and kept a small square dot over the i.
Dropping the old swoosh made the brand flatter and more digital.

logoResearch.name: AMD
logoResearch.verifiedFact: AMD designs processors and graphics chips.
observations: Wide black capitals are paired with an arrow-like symbol.
The symbol suggests direction and forward movement.

logoResearch.name: Dell
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Dell is an American computer and IT company.
observations: The tilted E is a famous detail from the company's early days.
A circle around the name turns it into a badge.

logoResearch.name: HP
logoResearch.verifiedFact: HP is a pioneer of personal computers and printers.
observations: Italic lowercase letters h and p sit inside a blue circle.
The slant adds movement to a very simple monogram.

logoResearch.name: Sony
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Sony is a Japanese electronics and entertainment company.
observations: The serif capitals have barely changed since 1973.
Its timeless, simple design has never needed a symbol.

logoResearch.name: Lenovo
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Lenovo is the world's largest PC maker.
observations: A bold red wordmark with rounded letters feels friendly and modern.
Lenovo often places the wordmark in a red box as its app-style icon.

logoResearch.name: Cisco
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Cisco is a networking and security company.
observations: The vertical bars recall the Golden Gate Bridge, a nod to the company's San Francisco roots.
They also read as electromagnetic signals, perfect for a networking brand.

logoResearch.name: Qualcomm
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Qualcomm designs chips for smartphones and wireless devices.
observations: A blue, rounded wordmark with linked m's at the end.
The connected letters echo the idea of wireless connections.

logoResearch.name: OpenAI
logoResearch.verifiedFact: OpenAI is the AI research company behind ChatGPT.
observations: The woven, flower-like symbol is built from interlocking curves.
A clean black wordmark keeps the brand calm and neutral.

logoResearch.name: Anthropic
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Anthropic is an AI safety company and the maker of Claude.
observations: Wide, evenly spaced capitals give the wordmark a calm, considered tone.
A slash replaces part of a letter, a small, technical detail.

logoResearch.name: Stripe
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Stripe is a payments platform used by millions of businesses.
observations: A bold, purple lowercase wordmark is the whole identity.
The color has become a signature of modern fintech design.

logoResearch.name: Figma
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Figma is a collaborative design tool, widely used by product teams.
observations: Five colorful shapes stack into an F.
The shapes echo the circles and rectangles designers draw in the tool.

logoResearch.name: Notion
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Notion is an all-in-one workspace for notes, docs, and projects.
observations: A serif N sits inside a hand-drawn box, like a note on paper.
Black and white keeps the brand minimal, like the product itself.

logoResearch.name: Linear
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Linear is project-tracking software for software teams.
observations: A circle filled with diagonal stripes suggests motion and progress.
A clean, simple wordmark matches the product's focus on speed.

logoResearch.name: Vercel
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Vercel is a cloud platform for front-end developers.
observations: A solid black triangle is one of the simplest logos in tech.
It suggests a peak, or an arrow pointing up, which fits a deployment platform.

logoResearch.name: Rippling
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Rippling makes HR, IT, and finance software for businesses.
observations: The symbol is made of repeating curves, like ripples spreading out.
Spaced capitals keep the wordmark tidy and professional.

logoResearch.name: Plaid
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Plaid connects apps to people's bank accounts behind the scenes.
observations: The symbol is a crisscross pattern, a literal take on the name.
Bold capitals keep the brand solid and trustworthy, important in finance.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 tech logos in one consistent format, grouped into Big Tech, software, consumer apps, hardware, and AI and startups.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the company's size or products.
sectionIntroductions: The biggest tech companies have some of the most recognizable logos in the world, most of them built around one simple symbol or one strong color.
Software companies sell something invisible, so their logos often use simple metaphors like a cloud, a box, or a shopping bag.
Consumer apps live on home screens, so their logos are designed to work first as a small, colorful app icon.
Hardware and chip makers lean on bold wordmarks and engineering-inspired details.
AI companies and newer startups favor minimal, often black-and-white identities that feel calm and precise.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of tech logos, not a ranking of companies.
Look at how each logo works as a tiny app icon and how much of it is symbol, color, or type.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo holds up when reduced to an app icon.

findings.heading: One shape beats a detailed illustration
findings.text: Apple, Vercel, and Meta prove that a single simple shape can carry a global brand on any screen.

findings.heading: Owning a color is a shortcut to recognition
findings.text: Spotify green, Netflix red, Stripe purple, and Snapchat yellow are recognizable even before you read the name.

findings.heading: Wordmarks keep getting simpler
findings.text: Uber, Intel, and Google have all simplified their wordmarks to work better on small, high-density screens.

findings.heading: AI brands are going quiet
findings.text: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Linear use black-and-white identities that feel calm and precise rather than flashy.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new tech logo
checklistItems: Does the logo still read as a 16-pixel favicon and an app icon?
Is there one simple, ownable shape?
Can you own a color in your category?
Does the wordmark work in light and dark mode?
Will it still feel right after your product changes?
